purpose: Electron desktop cockpit for driving Claude Code CLI sessions, organizing per-project work into Epics tracked from proposal through scheduled PRD execution.
what: The app centers on a **TAB → operations-root → EPIC → session** hierarchy: a Terminal tab is anchored to one project cwd, which owns a `session-manager-operations/` folder governed by a **single-writer law** (`opsOwnership.cjs`), and each Epic (`PromptSession`) is a 1:1 tagged `claude` session viewable as either Chat or Terminal.

Recent work (v0.53–v0.55) reworked Epic creation into two independent axes — **Agent** (`agentType`, a persona from the now-CRUD-editable Agent Library, `agentLibrary.cjs`/`AgentLibrary.tsx`) and **Tag** (mission: feature/bug/discussion, from `TagLibrary.tsx`) — with a many-to-many `tags:` frontmatter membership editable from either library page, both writing through `savePersona`.

The **Scheduler** is a browser over PRDs minted per-Epic (`scheduler/epics/<epic-id>/prds/`), run as capped-concurrency `claude -p` jobs with boot reconciliation, a dead-process reaper, and a definition-of-done gate that re-verifies completed PRDs' acceptance criteria at queue-drain.

A parallel design-import track (via `claude_design` MCP) is redesigning major surfaces — Libraries, Scheduler (Canvas-2/Almanac), Epics, Project Home — translating Figma-like `.jsx`/`.html` mocks into the renderer's component set.

Distribution is `npx claude-code-session-manager@latest` (Electron+node-pty rebuilt via postinstall), driven through an in-repo `/builder` skill that diffs git against the published npm package and decides version bumps.

scope: Scheduler formally scoped as a browser over TAB→EPIC→PRD; global scheduler bookkeeping retired in favor of per-project queue/state shards
conventions: Two-axis Epic creation is now real: `agentType` (who) and `tag` (mission/what) are separate, both editable via full CRUD Agent/Tag Library pages — never describe either library as read-only in new docs.

Every Epic is born `proposed`; `ensureEpic`/`createPromptSession` are structurally prevented from minting an `active` Epic directly — `proposed → active` has exactly one transition (Approve & start, or the New Epic first-prompt submit).
`active-index.json` writes must be read-merge-write, never a blind overwrite (past incident: lost Epics from concurrent writers).
Zustand selectors must return the raw stored slice, never a freshly-built array/object inline — three prior blank-app incidents (`lint:selectors` guards this).

Never shell out to `claude -p` without an explicit `--model` pin, and keep concurrent `claude -p` jobs capped at the configured slot pool (historically 3, discussed raising toward a configurable 0–10 default 5) to avoid OOM.
